title: Best-of-Both-Worlds Authenticated Encryption
summary: A related construction combines indifferentiability with standard-model collision resistance; the unresolved task is an authenticated-encryption scheme with indifferentiability and RAE security under a standard-model assumption.

formal_statement.body: Construct a best-of-both-worlds authenticated-encryption scheme that is simultaneously indifferentiable from an ideal primitive and $\mathrm{RAE}$-secure under a standard-model assumption. Such a combination is plausible because chop--Merkle--Damg$\mathring{a}$rd can be proved both indifferentiable from a random oracle and collision resistant in the standard model under standard assumptions; the unresolved task is to obtain an analogous joint guarantee for $\mathrm{RAE}$ security.

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption design combining indifferentiability with RAE security.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a scheme that is simultaneously indifferentiable from an ideal primitive and RAE-secure under a standard-model assumption.

progress.summary: The source presents a best-of-both-worlds construction as plausible, motivated by a construction with indifferentiability and standard-model collision resistance. It explicitly leaves the analogous RAE-security guarantee for future work.
citation_labels: Manuel Barbosa et al., Indifferentiable Authenticated Encryption
